steps.message:
The APK builds successfully. Here's a summary of the diagnosis and fix.

## Root cause

When a user imports only a **field** (`field_sample.csv`) but no **traits**, the Collect screen has an empty trait spinner. Two defects combine:

1. **`trait_counter.xml` had `android:visibility="visible"`** while every other trait layout defaults to `"gone"`. So the counter's `+1`/`-1` buttons were rendered on top of the Collect screen even though no trait was selected.
2. **`TraitBox.currentTrait` is only ever assigned inside the spinner's `onItemSelected` callback.** With an empty adapter that callback never fires, so `currentTrait` stayed `null`. Pressing `+1` hit `getCurrentTrait().getTrait()` → `NullPointerException` at `CounterTraitLayout$1.onClick` — exactly the reported trace.

The same null `currentTrait` also crashes the other Collect buttons the reporter mentioned (NA, delete, and the trait/entry arrows via `validateData()`), so I fixed those paths too.

## Changes

**`res/layout/trait_counter.xml`** — default visibility `visible` → `gone`, matching all other trait layouts. This is the primary fix: no orphan counter UI when nothing is selected.

**`traits/CounterTraitLayout.java`** — extracted the duplicated add/minus logic into `updateCounter(int step)` which returns early when `getCurrentTrait()` is `null`. `loadLayout()` and `deleteTraitListener()` are likewise null-guarded, and `parseCounterValue()` tolerates a non-numeric display value (e.g. a leftover `"NA"`), which was a latent `NumberFormatException`. Behavior for a real selected trait is unchanged.

**`activities/CollectActivity.java`** — hardened the null-`currentTrait` paths:
- `validateData()` dereferenced `currentTrait` on line 280 *before* its own existing `!= null` check three lines later — it now returns `true` early when nothing is selected (this alone fixed the entry/trait arrow crashes).
- The NA and delete toolbar click listeners return early instead of dereferencing null.
- `getCurrentFormat()` / `existsTrait()` are now null-safe.
- `initWidgets()` treats an *empty* trait array like a missing one and calls a new `TraitBox.clearTraits()`, which resets `currentTrait`, empties the spinner/details, hides all trait layouts and disables the value field — so no stale, clickable trait control can ever be left on screen.

## Build note

`./gradlew clean assembleDebug` fails in this environment during dependency resolution only — the sandbox blocks all outbound network, and `build.gradle` pins Firebase/Play-Services with the dynamic version `[17.4.1]`, which forces a remote `maven-metadata.xml` lookup on every run. This happens on the unmodified tree as well and is unrelated to the patch. Building against the local dependency cache with `./gradlew clean assembleDebug --offline` compiles and packages cleanly (`debug-4.3.3.apk`, 27 tasks, BUILD SUCCESSFUL).
